summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of gunshot wound to the spine resulting in paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter use presented with a one-week history of foul-smelling urine, fever, vomiting, and bilateral flank pain. She was admitted for presumed complicated urinary tract infection. Initial urinalysis showed nitrite positivity with moderate bacteria, and urine culture later confirmed Escherichia coli resistant to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. She was treated with antibiotics, and her symptoms improved during the hospital stay. Pain was managed with oral tramadol and acetaminophen, and she was discharged home on a revised antibiotic regimen with phenazopyridine for urinary discomfort. A primary care follow-up was scheduled to monitor culture results and ongoing care. The patient was stable at discharge, with resolved fever and improved pain control.
